column1: 1:1|In the third year of Jehoiakim king of Judah’s reign, Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came to Jerusalem and besieged it.|Keeps third-year dating without harmonizing chronology.

1:2|The Lord gave Jehoiakim king of Judah into his hand, along with some of the vessels from God’s house. He brought them to Shinar, to the house of his god, and placed the vessels in his god’s treasury.|Preserves Lord title, partial vessels and repeated god's house.
1:3|The king ordered Ashpenaz, chief of his eunuchs, to bring in some Israelites from the royal family and the nobility:|Retains eunuch designation with court-title note.

1:4|young men without any physical defect, handsome, skilled in every kind of wisdom, knowledgeable, discerning, and capable of serving in the king’s palace. They were to be taught the literature and language of the Chaldeans.|Keeps male selection and full qualifications.

1:5|The king assigned them a daily portion of his own food and the wine he drank. They were to be trained for three years, then enter the king’s service.|Preserves daily allotment and three-year period.
1:6|Among them were Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah, from Judah.|Keeps four Hebrew names and origin.
1:7|The chief eunuch gave them new names: Daniel he called Belteshazzar; Hananiah, Shadrach; Mishael, Meshach; and Azariah, Abed-nego.|Preserves each exact name pairing.

1:8|Daniel resolved not to defile himself with the king’s food or the wine he drank. He asked the chief eunuch for permission to avoid defiling himself.|Keeps defilement repeated without inventing motive.
1:9|God caused the chief eunuch to show Daniel kindness and compassion.|Preserves divine cause and paired favor terms.

1:10|But the chief eunuch told Daniel, “I am afraid of my lord the king, who assigned your food and drink. Why should he see you looking worse than the other young men your age? You would put my head at risk with the king.”|Keeps personal danger and comparative concern.
1:11|Daniel then spoke to the steward whom the chief eunuch had appointed over Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah:|Distinguishes steward from chief and repeats names.
1:12|“Please test your servants for ten days. Give us vegetables to eat and water to drink.|Keeps ten days and request, not dietary prescription.
1:13|Then compare our appearance with that of the young men eating the king’s food. Deal with your servants according to what you see.”|Preserves requested empirical comparison and discretion.
1:14|He agreed and tested them for ten days.|Retains explicit duration repetition.
1:15|At the end of ten days, they looked better and fuller in body than all the young men eating the king’s food.|Keeps fuller flesh rather than modern thinness ideal.
1:16|So the steward continued taking away their assigned food and wine and giving them vegetables.|Preserves ongoing substitution without inventing disposal.

1:17|God gave all four of these young men knowledge and insight into every kind of literature and wisdom. Daniel also understood visions and dreams of every kind.|Distinguishes shared gifts from Daniel's additional understanding.
1:18|When the time set by the king for bringing them in had ended, the chief eunuch presented them to Nebuchadnezzar.|Keeps appointed training endpoint.
1:19|The king spoke with them. Among them all, no one matched Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah, so they entered the king’s service.|Preserves four names and outcome.

1:20|In every matter of wisdom and understanding he asked about, the king found them ten times better than all the magicians and enchanters in his entire kingdom.|Keeps tenfold comparison and both specialist groups.
1:21|Daniel remained until the first year of King Cyrus.|Does not imply death at the stated endpoint.
2:1|In the second year of Nebuchadnezzar’s reign, Nebuchadnezzar had dreams. His spirit was troubled, and his sleep left him.|Keeps repeated name and difficult sleeplessness idiom.
2:2|The king ordered the magicians, enchanters, sorcerers, and Chaldeans summoned to tell him his dreams. They came and stood before the king.|Preserves four distinct court groups.
2:3|The king told them, “I have had a dream, and my spirit is troubled. I want to understand the dream.”|Keeps troubled spirit and knowing dream.
2:4|The Chaldeans answered the king in Aramaic, “May the king live forever! Tell your servant the dream, and we will explain its meaning.”|Retains language marker and singular read-form servant.

2:5|The king replied to the Chaldeans, “My decision is firm. If you do not tell me the dream and its meaning, you will be torn limb from limb and your houses reduced to refuse heaps.|Keeps decision reading and explicit bodily threat.
2:6|But if you tell me the dream and its meaning, you will receive gifts, rewards, and great honor from me. So tell me the dream and its meaning.”|Preserves repeated paired demand and three rewards.
2:7|They answered again, “Let the king tell his servants the dream, and we will explain its meaning.”|Keeps second request and plural servants.
2:8|The king replied, “I know for certain that you are buying time, because you see that my decision is firm.|Retains buying-time idiom and repeated firmness.

2:9|If you do not tell me the dream, there is only one sentence for you. You have agreed to tell me lying, corrupt words until the situation changes. So tell me the dream, and I will know you can explain its meaning.”|Keeps test of interpretation and alleged collusion.

2:10|The Chaldeans answered the king, “No one on earth can do what the king asks. No king, however great and powerful, has ever asked such a thing of any magician, enchanter, or Chaldean.|Preserves universal impossibility claim and specialist list.
2:11|What the king asks is difficult. No one can reveal it to the king except the gods, who do not dwell with flesh.”|Keeps divine/human dwelling contrast without endorsing speakers.
2:12|At this the king became furious and ordered all Babylon’s wise men destroyed.|Retains indiscriminate lethal command.
2:13|The decree went out, and the wise men were being put to death. They also sought Daniel and his companions to kill them.|Preserves participial execution language with timing note.
2:14|Then Daniel responded with counsel and tact to Arioch, the king’s chief executioner, who had gone out to kill Babylon’s wise men.|Keeps executioner's actual function and Daniel's manner.
2:15|He asked Arioch, the king’s officer, “Why is the king’s decree so harsh?” Arioch explained the matter to Daniel.|Uses harsh with urgent alternative noted.
2:16|Daniel went in and asked the king to give him time, so he could explain the dream’s meaning to the king.|Keeps requested time despite accusation of delay.
2:17|Then Daniel went home and explained the matter to his companions Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah.|Retains Hebrew names in private setting.
2:18|He urged them to ask the God of heaven for mercy concerning this mystery, so Daniel and his companions would not perish with the rest of Babylon’s wise men.|Keeps mercy and shared peril.
2:19|During the night the mystery was revealed to Daniel in a vision. Then Daniel blessed the God of heaven.|Preserves night vision rather than recasting as dream.

2:20|Daniel said:
“May God’s name be blessed
from age to age,
for wisdom and power belong to him.|Keeps poetic praise and paired divine gifts.

2:21|He changes times and seasons;
he removes kings and raises up kings.
He gives wisdom to the wise
and knowledge to those with understanding.|Retains four parallel divine actions.
2:22|He reveals deep and hidden things;\nhe knows what is in the darkness,\nand light dwells with him.|Keeps revelation and light/dark contrast.

2:23|God of my ancestors, I thank and praise you.
You have given me wisdom and power;
now you have made known to me what we asked of you.
You have made the king’s matter known to us.”|Preserves me/we/us shifts and repeated knowing.

2:24|So Daniel went to Arioch, whom the king had appointed to destroy Babylon’s wise men. He told him, “Do not destroy Babylon’s wise men. Bring me before the king, and I will explain the meaning to him.”|Keeps rescue extending beyond Daniel's companions.
2:25|Arioch hurried Daniel before the king and said, “I have found a man among the exiles from Judah who can explain the meaning to the king.”|Preserves Arioch's claim as his own speech.
2:26|The king asked Daniel, whose name was Belteshazzar, “Can you tell me the dream I saw and its meaning?”|Keeps both names and paired question.
2:27|Daniel answered the king, “No wise men, enchanters, magicians, or diviners can reveal to the king the mystery he asks about.|Preserves four groups' inability.

2:28|But there is a God in heaven who reveals mysteries. He has shown King Nebuchadnezzar what will happen in days to come. This was your dream, the visions that passed through your mind as you lay in bed:|Keeps revelation source and future language without date scheme.
2:29|As you lay in bed, O king, thoughts came to you about what would happen afterward. The revealer of mysteries has shown you what will happen.|Retains repeated future revelation.

2:30|This mystery was revealed to me because the king was to be told its meaning and understand the thoughts of his heart, not because I have more wisdom than anyone else alive.|Preserves denial of personal superiority and revelatory purpose.
2:31|“You looked, O king, and there stood a great statue. This immense statue was dazzling, standing before you, terrifying to behold.|Keeps size, brilliance and terror distinct.
2:32|Its head was fine gold; its chest and arms were silver; its belly and thighs were bronze;|Preserves body-to-metal sequence.
2:33|its legs were iron, and its feet partly iron and partly clay.|Keeps mixed feet after iron legs.
2:34|As you watched, a stone was cut out without hands. It struck the statue on its iron-and-clay feet and crushed them.|Retains unmentioned cutting agent and point of impact.

2:35|Then the iron, clay, bronze, silver, and gold were crushed together and became like chaff on summer threshing floors. The wind carried them away, leaving no trace. But the stone that struck the statue became a great mountain and filled the whole earth.|Preserves full material list and agricultural simile.
2:36|“That was the dream. Now we will tell the king its meaning.|Retains plural we without inventing co-speakers.
2:37|You, O king, are king of kings. The God of heaven has given you the kingdom, power, strength, and honor.|Keeps four gifts and source of kingship.

2:38|Wherever human beings live, he has given them into your hand, along with the beasts of the field and birds of the sky, making you ruler over them all. You are the head of gold.|Preserves nonhuman dominion and explicit sole identification.
2:39|After you another kingdom will arise, inferior to yours. Then a third kingdom, of bronze, will rule the whole earth.|Keeps kingdoms unnamed and ordinal sequence.

2:40|A fourth kingdom will be strong as iron. As iron crushes and shatters everything, and like iron that breaks all these things, it will crush and break them.|Preserves repeated destructive iron comparison.

2:41|You saw feet and toes partly of potter’s clay and partly of iron. The kingdom will be divided, yet some of iron’s strength will remain in it, just as you saw iron mixed with clay.|Keeps divided composition and residual strength.
2:42|As the toes were partly iron and partly clay, the kingdom will be partly strong and partly brittle.|Preserves proportion without inventing number of rulers.

2:43|As you saw iron mixed with clay, they will mingle through human offspring, but they will not hold together, just as iron does not mix with clay.|Keeps seed-of-humans phrase with marriage alternative noted.

2:44|In the days of those kings, the God of heaven will establish a kingdom that will never be destroyed or handed over to another people. It will crush all these kingdoms and bring them to an end, but it will stand forever.|Preserves permanence and destructive replacement.

2:45|That is why you saw a stone cut from the mountain without hands, crushing iron, bronze, clay, silver, and gold. The great God has shown the king what will happen afterward. The dream is certain, and its meaning is trustworthy.”|Keeps mountain detail and changed material-list order.
2:46|Then King Nebuchadnezzar fell facedown and bowed before Daniel. He ordered an offering and incense presented to him.|Preserves honor directed at Daniel without invented refusal.
2:47|The king told Daniel, “Truly, your God is God of gods and Lord of kings, a revealer of mysteries, since you could reveal this mystery.”|Keeps king's confession and plural your.

2:48|Then the king promoted Daniel, gave him many great gifts, made him ruler over the whole province of Babylon, and appointed him chief over all Babylon’s wise men.|Preserves four acts of promotion.

2:49|At Daniel’s request the king appointed Shadrach, Meshach, and Abed-nego over the affairs of Babylon’s province. Daniel remained at the king’s court.|Keeps companions' appointments distinct from Daniel's location.
